headline: Five CRITICALs are live in the shipped product. Two are navigation dead ends - signed-in users cannot reach /guide, /terms or /privacy at all, and six CTAs on those very pages render a blank white screen. One is a measured WCAG failure (1.31:1 against a 4.5:1 floor). Two silently destroy user data: a nested settings write discards its siblings, and an idempotency key charge() accepts and never uses means a retried settlement bills twice. And one thing this audit still does NOT know: the IDOR sweep was never run (SEC-OPEN-A), so object-level authorisation across the API is unknown rather than clean - the largest remaining unknown, and this repo has produced exactly that class of bug before.

findings.title: Shallow merge in update_user_settings silently destroys nested keys

evidence.observed: MEASURED with deepcopy so aliasing cannot mask it: applying {'ai':{'detection':{'enabled':True}}} onto {'ai':{'detection':{'enabled':False,'min_human':70,'paid_verification':'off'}}} yields {'enabled':True}. LOST KEYS: ['min_human','paid_verification']. `current[k].update(v)` merges exactly one level, so a two-level write replaces its whole subtree.

findings.impact: A user who sets a detection threshold and later toggles detection loses the threshold, silently. The same defect is already documented on the CLIENT (SettingsApp.mergeSettings), so fixing one side alone leaves the data loss. It also makes any two-level scoped-override write destructive.

fix.approach: Deep-merge dicts recursively. `scoped` stays REPLACE_ON_WRITE (it is a document), so the recursion must respect that opt-out.

REPLACE_ON_WRITE = frozenset({"scoped"})


def _deep_merge(base: dict, patch: dict) -> dict:
    """Merge dicts recursively. Scalars and LISTS replace.

    Lists replace rather than append deliberately: these are configuration values
    (style samples, enabled detectors) and appending would make removal impossible -
    the same reason `scoped` is REPLACE_ON_WRITE.
    """
    out = dict(base or {})
    for k, v in (patch or {}).items():
        if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(out.get(k), dict):
            out[k] = _deep_merge(out[k], v)
        else:
            out[k] = copy.deepcopy(v)
    return out

findings.title: A blocking urlopen with a 4 second timeout runs inside an async request handler

evidence.observed: MEASURED by reading the call chain. fetch_store_version (line 81) is a plain `def` that calls urllib.request.urlopen with timeout=4, and it is called from `async def get_extension_version` (line 211). urllib is synchronous and the call is not offloaded, so the coroutine blocks the single event loop for up to four seconds on every cache miss - during which NO other request is served.

findings.impact: One slow or unresponsive Chrome Web Store endpoint stalls the entire API for up to 4 s per request, not just the version check. On a single-process uvicorn (which is what this box runs) that is a self-inflicted DoS whenever the store is slow, and it is reached from the extension's own update check.

fix.approach: Offload the blocking call to a thread. Keep fetch_store_version synchronous - it is correct as a function; only its CALL SITE is wrong.

# Blocking here is invisible to a correctness assertion, so measure concurrency.
import asyncio, time
from unittest.mock import patch


def test_version_check_does_not_block_the_event_loop(client):
    def slow_store_call():
        time.sleep(1.5)          # stands in for a slow store lookup
        return "9.9.9"

    async def concurrent_probe():
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        task = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(
            lambda: client.get("/api/extension/version")))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
        await asyncio.to_thread(
            lambda: client.get("/api/health"))   # must return WHILE the first is in flight
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
        await task
        return elapsed

    with patch("server.routes_extension.fetch_store_version", slow_store_call):
        elapsed = asyncio.run(concurrent_probe())
    assert elapsed < 1.4, (
        f"health probe was delayed to {elapsed:.2f}s - the store call is blocking the loop")

The boundary is documented in api_keys.require_session_auth - the check is that every account-critical route calls it, and that the call is ORDERED after get_current_user (calling it first reads request.state.auth_via_api_key before auth sets it, which let a key mint another key at HTTP 200).

decisions.subject: Tier allowances and the margin model
decisions.ruling: Tier allowances stay as they are: basic 30,000 / pro 100,000 / elite 270,000, trial 15,000, testing 10,000. The owner's intent is a mathematically ensured profit margin per tier, because the token unit is 1/100 of a cent.
decisions.consequence: The BALANCE IS THE CEILING. Never add a plan-based charge exemption. A negative balance is honest and self-blocks the account until a top-up; that is the design, not a bug.
decisions.standing_hazard: plan == 'elite' bypasses are a RECURRING class in this codebase - removed at least twice and found alive again in routes_dump.py. It is why ECON-04 is listed as a sweep, not a one-line fix.

decisions.subject: Refunding is earn-only
decisions.ruling: Tokens are consumed, not refunded. Nothing is charged before the work runs, so a task that fails outright is simply never charged - there is nothing to refund.
decisions.consequence: The pre-flight gate checks eligibility only (has_usage_balance) and takes no money. Settlement charges the measured cost after the fact (ledger_watermark -> usage_cents_since -> charge_actual_usage). The old up-front charge plus refund branch was deleted because with nothing charged, a refund would MINT a free token.
decisions.consequence_of_removing_it: Test TASK-02's assertions were rewritten to the new semantics: a session that failed outright, or disconnected before doing real work and collected nothing, is simply never charged; a session that ran steps and then disconnected still pays for what it used.

durable_notes.lesson: with_for_update() IS A NO-OP ON SQLITE
durable_notes.detail: Verified by compiling the statement: the emitted SQL contains no FOR UPDATE. Any fix whose whole approach is 'add with_for_update()' is INERT on this database - it will pass review, pass tests, and change nothing. Two mechanisms actually work: BEGIN IMMEDIATE (serialises a read-modify-write) and json_set/json_extract in a single statement (atomic with no lock).
durable_notes.why_it_matters: REL-01 is money. The obvious fix was the wrong one.

durable_notes.lesson: A read-then-write on the JSON settings blob cannot be fixed by locking advice - the change must go INSIDE the statement
durable_notes.detail: Measured: two concurrent 400-token debits against a balance of 1000 left 600 before the fix (one debit swallowed) and 200 after (credits.debit_tokens_atomic).
durable_notes.why_it_matters: The same shape recurs wherever settings.token_balance is read, modified and written.

durable_notes.lesson: A test double that ignores the write proves nothing
durable_notes.detail: The first merge test passed straight through the REL-02 bug because its fake DB never applied db.execute(...). The double must capture AND apply the statement.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: This is how a green suite coexists with a live defect - TEST-01, TEST-02 and TEST-07 are the same family.

durable_notes.lesson: The test DB is a persistent FILE
durable_notes.detail: conftest points at sqlite:///./test_helpotron.db with no per-test rollback, so an assertion on an exact global row count breaks in a full-suite run because the previous run's rows are still there. Use a unique public_id / idempotency key per run.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: Three v1 tests failed only in full-suite runs for exactly this reason. TEST-05 is the durable fix; the uuid workaround is a symptom.

durable_notes.detail: is_unmetered() is operator-only by construction (security.is_admin_user); its docstring records that the elite short-circuit was removed once and survived anyway.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: A paid tier consuming unbounded upstream spend was live in routes_dump.py until v1.

durable_notes.lesson: create_all() does NOT add an index to a table that already exists
durable_notes.detail: Model-declared index=True only helps a fresh DB. Measured now: 70 index=True declarations against exactly 1 CREATE INDEX statement, so the live DB carries almost none of them.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: REL-05, and it is why every new UNIQUE constraint (REL-03) needs an explicit idempotent CREATE INDEX in the migration block.

durable_notes.lesson: A feature can be 100% implemented and 100% dead
durable_notes.detail: The avatar endpoint existed with no caller. CONV-02 is the same class: seven study-material export endpoints with zero frontend callers.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: Grep for a CALLER, not just for the code. A passing test over an endpoint proves the endpoint works, not that anyone can reach it.

durable_notes.detail: Tokens = usage, in settings.token_balance (a JSON blob, not a column). Credits = earned-only discounts, in users.discount_balance + discount_spillover, created solely by earn_credits, applied as a percent discount on an order.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: UI-05 is exactly this confusion in the UI - the CREDITS label renders token_balance.

durable_notes.lesson: The server is the only config that counts - server/.env is a decoy
durable_notes.detail: Nothing reads server/.env. server/config.py:15 sets env_file to the REPO ROOT, and server/llm.py:18 load_dotenv()s the same root file with override=True. A key put in server/.env is present-but-inert, which is indistinguishable from working until you read it back through the app.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: A rotation was performed into server/.env and had no effect. Also why TURNSTILE_* looked configurable while the gate was off.

durable_notes.lesson: Duplicate auth logic is how a new credential type gets forgotten
durable_notes.detail: Two live instances were found: routes_features.get_current_authenticated_user had its own copy of the cookie/JWT/session logic and never learned about API keys; routes_organization had its own cookie-only get_current_user. Both now delegate to the shared resolver.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: Before declaring a credential done, grep for EVERY place that parses Authorization.

durable_notes.lesson: Never restart a live service as your verification
durable_notes.detail: Order is edit -> ast.parse/import check -> suite -> restart -> verify the endpoint. The suite imports server.main, so it catches a SyntaxError in a second. A restart against a broken file turns a syntax error into an outage, and Restart=always then hides it as 'activating' while it crash-loops (81 restarts, presented as a login failure).
durable_notes.why_it_matters: This took the production site down once already.

durable_notes.lesson: A test that bypasses the link that is broken will pass forever
durable_notes.detail: Round 1 of the scroll fix drove executeReturnedActions directly and stubbed the server; the real path is model -> fenced block -> server validation -> control_actions -> executor. The harness proved nothing about delivery.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: When a feature spans client and server, the repro must go through BOTH.

execution_order.theme: Stop the data loss and the blank screens
execution_order.rationale: Two of these silently destroy user data or money; two make the product unusable for a signed-in user. Fix them before anything cosmetic.

execution_order.theme: Stop the product lying to the user
execution_order.rationale: CONV-01 hands a user a fabricated BIO-309 assignment and reports success; LEG-01 is the highest-consequence finding in the audit; UI-05 mislabels a balance. TEST-08 and UI-09 are one-liners that ride along.

execution_order.theme: Unblock work that is already built
execution_order.rationale: Highest value per hour in the whole plan: the export suite, the triage workflow and the orphan cleanup are already implemented or already dead. This is wiring and deletion.

Five independent blocking calls in async handlers, all on the API's hot paths, all one-line fixes once located. They are grouped because they share one test shape (a concurrency probe) and one reviewer.
This box has frozen twice. These four determine whether it happens a third time. EFF-07 is the guard that does not guard; EFF-02 is 2.16 GiB idle.

DSGN-01 and DSGN-04 are verified and user-visible (an unreadable label; a third-party request from a self-hosted app). The rest are drift and should be swept in one pass with DSGN-01's contrast work rather than four separate ones.

ECON-04's report claimed ~12 bypass sites and only 2 were verified and fixed. Sweep the rest, then settle ECON-05 (are the surviving flat prices floors or the whole charge) and REL-05's index migration.

TEST-05 is the leverage: a per-test rollback removes the uuid workaround from every test that carries it AND removes a class of run-order flakes. The others are tests that cannot fail for the reason they name - and they are only provable once the DB is isolated.

execution_order.theme: Compliance copy and the open unknowns
execution_order.rationale: Copy goes last because it must describe the product AFTER the fixes land, not before. The three SEC open items are unknown, not clean - SEC-OPEN-A (IDOR) is the largest single unknown in the audit and should be run early if capacity allows, but it is placed here because it is a sweep rather than a fix.

open_questions.question: Should /pricing for a signed-in user open the Plans tab of Credits & Billing, or a public pricing page?
open_questions.blocks: UI-01, UI-02 (both need to map a destination)
open_questions.recommendation: Credits -> Plans tab; the component already reads GET /api/plans.

open_questions.question: Is the 'signup' navigation key meant to open the auth modal or to scroll to the landing page's signup section?
open_questions.recommendation: Open the auth modal - a mapped view silently swallows the intent to authenticate.

open_questions.question: Should HIP (2.16 GiB idle) become demand-driven, accepting a model-load delay on the first request after an idle stop?
open_questions.recommendation: Yes, with a 15-minute idle window. The RAM is the scarcer resource on this box, and hip_humanizer already degrades to the documented fallback path when the endpoint is unreachable.

open_questions.question: Are the surviving flat prices deliberate floors or stale absolute prices?
open_questions.recommendation: Floors. AGENTS.md records the floor as deliberate - 'cost drives the price up; the flat price stays as a floor because some real work consumes platform resources that never reach the LLM ledger'. The finding must then be narrowed to naming which floors no longer bind.

open_questions.question: Does the owner want a legal entity named in the Terms, and if so which?
open_questions.recommendation: Owner decision. Inventing an entity name into a legal document would be worse than the gap - do not edit legal copy unilaterally.

open_questions.question: Should the public site be paused? It is currently serving the full app, and the owner's 09-17 instruction was to keep the paused banner.
open_questions.blocks: LEG-05 mentions the paused state as a fact; the extension's /releases and /version currently 503 because the public site is intended to be paused.
open_questions.recommendation: Confirm with the owner before 'fixing' anything here - the mismatch is between the running state and the instruction, and only the owner can resolve which is intended.

open_questions.question: Should the seven study-material exports surface on the material card, or in a batch 'export all' control?
open_questions.recommendation: Per-material, next to the material they export. A batch control invites a download of everything, which is a different feature.
